title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Fire Protection"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Fire protection asks how much wildfire damage is avoided because fires do not persist as strongly
where nature dominates. The calculation is ported function by function from the GEP wildfire
repository's R pipeline, `gep_wildfire_2019.R`. The base year is 2019 and the price convention
recorded in `es_config.csv` is `avoided damage`.

## Quantity

Burned acres avoided or added in 2019.

The persistence side comes from per-country AR(1) regressions of burned area on its own one-year
lag, run upstream with the results committed as a CSV. `build_regression_type_ids` filters the
regressions the GEP does not read and assigns each remaining one a type id.
`compute_beta_differences` then reads three quantities off the wide table:

- the baseline persistence effect, total burned area on its own lag over the full sample,
- the nature-versus-human cause difference, nature-caused fires' persistence minus human-caused
  fires',
- the nature-versus-human area difference, persistence in nature-dominated minus human-dominated
  districts.

The two differences use `difference_stats`, which takes the difference of two independent
estimates, combines their standard errors in quadrature, and reports the two-sided normal
approximation p-value. A difference is computed only where all four inputs are present.

`compute_avoided_acres` converts each beta to marginal additional acres by multiplying by
`HA_TO_ACRES`, then to 2019 additional acres by multiplying by the country's 2018 burned hectares.

## Price

EM-DAT wildfire damages per burned acre, by country. `read_emdat_wildfire_damages` sums the total
adjusted damage column, which the source workbook stores in thousands of USD with comma
separators, over wildfire events per ISO3. `compute_damage_per_acre` divides that by the country's
burned acres across all panel years and fills any country whose rate is zero or missing with the
global average over countries with positive rates.

## Valuation

`compute_gep` multiplies the two together and flips the sign, because additional acres carry the
persistence sign and the value of avoiding them is the negative product:

$$
\text{GEP}_{\text{variant}} = -\,\text{additional acres 2019}_{\text{variant}} \times \text{damages per acre}
$$

Countries absent from the damage-rate merge take the global average, as in the source.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, scoped to the `fire_protection` service:

- `fire_regression_results_path`, the committed per-country AR(1) regression results.
- `fire_emdat_path`, the EM-DAT custom request workbook.
- `fire_panel_path`, the ADM2 burned-area panel, with a `_source_note` row recording that it comes
  from the drive's Wildfires folder.

`reference/GEP_wildfire_2019_results.csv` ships inside the module as the frozen replication
anchor.

## Outputs

`beta_differences.csv`, `avoided_acres.csv` and `damage_per_acre.csv`, each from its own task,
then two files from `gep_calculation`. `fire_protection_2019_results.csv` keeps the source repo's
column shape so it can be diffed against the committed output. `gep_by_country_base_year.csv`
holds the r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, the three variant columns
`GEP_wildfire_2019_baseline`, `GEP_wildfire_2019_nn_hh` and `GEP_wildfire_2019_ttn_tth`, and
`fire_protection_gep`. All three variant totals are logged.

`GID_0` is already an iso3 country label, so the r250 attributes join by label and nothing is
summed in the collapse.

## Method constants

- `HA_TO_ACRES = 2.47105`.
- `FIRE_BASELINE_ID = 3`, `FIRE_NN_ID = 2` and `FIRE_HH_ID = 1`, `FIRE_TTN_ID = 6` and
  `FIRE_TTH_ID = 7`, which select the betas for the three variants.
- `FIRE_DROP_Y_VARS`, the fifteen days, counts and average variants the source drops before ids
  are assigned.
- `FIRE_GEP_PROVISIONAL_VARIANT = 'nn_hh'` in the tasks module, the variant
  `fire_protection_gep` currently carries.
- `significance_level` thresholds, 3 stars below p 0.01, 2 below 0.05, 1 below 0.10, otherwise 0.

`FIRE_REG_TYPES` records the five regression-type ids the GEP reads together with the
`(Y_var, Key_X_var, sample)` triple each id must carry.

| id | Y_var | Key_X_var | sample |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `total_ba_ha_human` | `L1_total_ba_ha_human` | full |
| 2 | `total_ba_ha_nature` | `L1_total_ba_ha_nature` | full |
| 3 | `total_burned_areas_ha` | `L1_total_burned_areas_ha` | full |
| 6 | `total_burned_areas_ha` | `L1_total_burned_areas_ha` | nature_subsample |
| 7 | `total_burned_areas_ha` | `L1_total_burned_areas_ha` | human_subsample |

## Faithful-port notes

Two behaviours are reproduced rather than corrected, so the port stays comparable against the
anchor.

The source pivots the regression table with a mean aggregator over every value column, including
the character significance stars. R's `mean()` on character returns NA, so every wide significance
column, and therefore every `*_signif_level` in the output, is 0 by construction. The p-value
columns beside them are real.

Beta selection is by regression-type id, which in the source is `data.table`'s `.GRP`, the
first-appearance order of the triple in the input CSV. A reordered input would silently reassign
the betas, so `build_regression_type_ids` asserts the expected triples and raises before any beta
is read.

## Taken as given

The AR(1) regressions themselves, which are run upstream and consumed here as a committed results
table. The committed per-country output reproduces to the float, which the test suite pins.

## What is open

Which of the three variants is the account's fire protection value. Baseline and
nature-versus-human cause both total negative globally, so the choice sets both the number and its
interpretation. `fire_protection_gep` defaults to the nature-versus-human cause difference
provisionally.

The ADM2 burned-area panel is not staged, and its own README says it lives on the drive. Until it
arrives, the 2018 burned areas and the damage rates are read from the frozen reference output,
with a loud log line each time, so the beta science and everything downstream still run and verify
on any machine.
